label: a lady of middle age in day dress out of doors, 1900s
note: Gathered 2026-11-07 for T-3447, Frances M. Glessner's day dress. None is of Chicago, the Glessner household or Frances Glessner, and no portrait of her has been read. The Met's 1902 suit is a real garment, photographed in colour on a dress form, and gives the cut and the black; Johnston's photograph shows women of fifty and more wearing such dress and hats out of doors; the Easter plate shows how they read in the street. A reference set says what a woman of this role and decade looked like, never what Frances Glessner wore on a given day.

pictures.name: met_1902_suit_coat
pictures.from: The Met open-access image CI50.108c_F.jpg (2166 x 3111), whole, reduced to 1600 high
pictures.caption: Black wool coat over the suit's lace-collared bodice, on a form. Suit, French, 1902 (The Met, C.I.50.108a-c)
pictures.shows: The coat from the front: black wool to the upper thigh, lapels, buttoned below the bust, braid at the cuffs and hem; the bodice's cream lace front and collar showing in its opening.

pictures.name: met_1902_suit_skirt
pictures.from: The Met open-access image CI50.108b_F.jpg (2240 x 3168), whole, reduced to 1600 high
pictures.caption: The suit's black gored skirt, on a hanger. Suit, French, 1902 (The Met, C.I.50.108a-c)
pictures.shows: A black wool skirt of gores, close at the waist and hips, flaring from about the knee to a wide hem, braid where the seams meet the hem.

pictures.name: met_1902_suit_bodice
pictures.from: The Met open-access image CI50.108a_F.jpg (2412 x 2951), whole, reduced to 1600 high
pictures.caption: The suit's black bodice with its lace yoke and standing collar. Suit, French, 1902 (The Met, C.I.50.108a-c)
pictures.shows: A black bodice pouched in front, a cream lace yoke and a tall lace standing collar tied with a ribbon, braided revers and tassels at the waist.

pictures.name: johnston_fairbanks_near
pictures.from: LOC TIFF 39000u.tif (6064 x 4840), crop [3600, 600, 4950, 2350], Mrs. Fairbanks at the stand, reduced to 1600 high
pictures.caption: Mrs. Fairbanks speaking at the Memorial Continental Hall cornerstone. F. B. Johnston, 1905-08 (LOC 2015647074)
pictures.shows: A matron standing at about five metres: a dark coat open over a pale front, a lace jabot from a high collar, frills at the wrists, a large hat heaped with pale plumes over drawn-up hair.

pictures.name: johnston_matrons_near
pictures.from: LOC TIFF 39000u.tif (6064 x 4840), crop [2050, 1450, 4100, 2400], the seated women beside the stand, at full resolution
pictures.caption: Older women seated beside the speakers' stand. F. B. Johnston, 1905-08 (LOC 2015647074)
pictures.shows: Women of fifty and more, head and shoulders, at about five metres: dark bodices, high white collars or lace at the throat, hats trimmed with flowers and feathers worn high on drawn-up hair.

pictures.name: detroit_1904_easter
pictures.from: LOC TIFF 4a11545u.tif (5166 x 4070), crop [1050, 2650, 2750, 4000], the walk at the lower left of the plate, reduced to 1600 wide
pictures.caption: Easter crowds on Fifth Avenue, New York, from above. Detroit Publishing Co., 1904 (LOC 2016803615)
pictures.shows: Women and men walking at ten to twenty metres: the women in long dark coats and skirts to the ground, some with pale fronts, nearly all in broad hats trimmed high; a woman reads as a dark bell, a pale collar and face, and a hat.
